claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by low-temperature SPS or severe plastic deformation can produce a sub-50 nm dual-phase solid solution in Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V without brittle intermetallics.
A VEC range of 4.4 to 4.8 favors a dual-phase BCC+BCC or BCC+FCC solid-solution constitution.
Values of atomic-size mismatch below 6.6% and Ω above 1 favor BCC solid-solution formation in HEAs.
Restricting Cr or Ti to below 2 at% prevents Laves-phase formation in the proposed refractory alloy.
Kinetic suppression of phase separation during consolidation stabilizes a metastable dual-phase disordered solid solution rather than an ordered intermetallic.
Coherent or semi-coherent dual-phase interfaces provide strain accommodation and reduce the brittleness typical of single-phase refractory HEAs.
An equiatomic or near-equiatomic Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V powder is prone to brittle single-phase BCC or intermetallic formation in the cast state.
Mechanical alloying for 20-40 hours induces severe plastic deformation and solid-solution formation.
SPS at 800-1000 °C or post-consolidation high-pressure torsion retains grains below 50 nm without phase decomposition.
SPS at 50-100 MPa under vacuum or inert gas followed by rapid quenching preserves the proposed metastable phases.
The resulting structure has grains below 50 nm and coherent or semi-coherent boundaries between BCC-rich and BCC-depleted, or BCC and FCC, solid solutions.
High configurational entropy stabilizes solid solutions while low-temperature SPS or SPD prevents brittle-intermetallic nucleation and grain growth.
The second solid-solution phase forms through controlled spinodal-like decomposition or nucleation driven by local compositional fluctuations.
Hall-Petch grain-boundary strengthening and solid-solution strengthening increase hardness and yield strength.
Dual-phase interfaces obstruct dislocation motion without causing the brittleness associated with ordered intermetallics.
The proposed nanocrystalline dual-phase state will have yield strength above 1500 MPa, hardness above 500 Hv, and fracture strain above 10%.
No Laves, sigma, or other brittle intermetallic phase will be detectable by XRD or TEM in the proposed state.
Cast NbMoTaW typically has a single BCC phase, grains above 10 µm, yield strength of about 800-1000 MPa, and brittle room-temperature fracture.
The proposed dual-phase nanostructure becomes unstable above 1100 °C because of grain coarsening and intermetallic precipitation.
The structure becomes unstable below VEC 4.4 or above VEC 5.0, and more than 2 at% Cr or Ti may trigger Laves-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says consolidation should suppress phase separation, whereas the mechanism says the desired second phase arises through controlled spinodal-like decomposition or second-phase nucleation. The distinction between suppressing unwanted decomposition and permitting desired decomposition is not defined.

The experiment includes VEC values outside 4.4-4.8 and Cr/Ti contents up to 5 at%, which the boundary field already identifies as potentially unstable, yet the rule states that an intermetallic in any sample falsifies the hypothesis.

The predicted thresholds are yield strength above 1500 MPa and fracture strain above 10%, but falsification is only triggered below 1200 MPa or 5%, leaving broad outcomes that fail the prediction without formally falsifying it.
